newsitem.title: BERMUDA: FIGURE SKATING-FEDERATION CHIEF WOULD SAYS JUDGING GUILTY.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-FEDERATION CHIEF WOULD SAYS JUDGING GUILTY.

text.p: International Skating Union president Ottavio Cinquanta says changes must be made in the system of judging the popular sport but that a solution is elusive.

Cinquanta, here for the Champions Series finals, spoke Friday about the vagaries of the current system which saw Russia's Alexei Urmanov catapult from sixth to first at the '97 European championships after the final skater, who did not win a medal himself.
"We have to produce a mathematical system that this will not happen. When you finish your performance and you are ranked in front of a skater you have to retain that position," said Cinquanta.
"In all sport disciplines where there is (subjective) judging, it's very difficult. If some expert is available to give us a perfect system, we will send him a bottle of champagne and flowers."

Cinquanta defended the judges themselves. "Each of the nine judges has a right to an opinion. It gives a wider sense of democracy but also produces some complications. The current system is good but everything can be improved," he said.

Although the ISU chief suggested that a new system could be in place for the '98 Winter Olympics in Nagano, Japan, the chair of ISU's Figure Skating Technical Committee expressed opposition to the idea.
"I don't think the Olympics is the place to experiment with a new system," said Sally Stapleford, who also heads the British skating association.

The technical committee will also investigate the use of video replays so judges can review the required elements a skater performs in the short programme segment of an event. Cinquanta said this would not be easy given each of the nine judges might wish to review one or more different elements.
The ISU council next meets in Prague in June.

Cinquanta also announced that the ISU will spend $1 million to launch and stage the new Junior Series competitions for skaters who are eligible to compete in the Junior worlds. In its first year, the Series will feature six events and a final.
